item.title: you must install .NET Desktop Runtime torun this application.
item.author: JaylanCharles

judgment.rationale: Multiple public reports and a .NET host trace show WinUI3Apps apphosts failing because required self-contained runtime files are missing beside the WinUI3Apps executables; Scoop fixed the same layout by copying hardlinks.txt entries, and origin/main contains matching installer copy logic.
evidence: Settings, Quick Access, and Peek show the runtime prompt even when Desktop Runtime 10 is installed.
ScoopInstaller/Extras#18020 was linked and a reporter confirmed force-updating Scoop resolved the popup.
A public host trace shows PowerToys.Settings.exe treated as self-contained and failing to find hostpolicy.dll.
Later comments report similar symptoms on Chocolatey/manual/winget and v0.101.2432.0.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve installer/package validation for WinUI3Apps hardlinks.txt copy/repair coverage, then ask affected reporters to retest a build with that repair.

fix_assessment.rationale: PowerToys should own installer/upgrade repair while package managers consume the same manifest; current reports need channel/build confirmation.

proposed_fixes.title: Repair missing WinUI3Apps runtime-file copies
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Some install or upgrade paths leave files listed by WinUI3Apps/hardlinks.txt absent from WinUI3Apps, so self-contained WinUI apphosts fall back to global dotnet probing and fail hostpolicy resolution.
plan: Ensure CreateWinAppSDKHardlinksCA runs for fresh install, upgrade, and repair.
Copy every hardlinks.txt entry from install root to WinUI3Apps when target is missing or stale.
Keep containment/UTF-8 validation and avoid hard-links because shared DACLs can break low-integrity preview handlers.
Add package validation that apphost runtime/deps files are either installed directly or listed in hardlinks.txt.
verification: Upgrade from 0.99.x/0.100.x and launch Settings, Quick Access, and Peek without a .NET prompt.
Validate package-manager extraction/update has the complete WinUI3Apps copy set.

confidence.rationale: Host trace and workaround directly match the failure; latest affected build/channel still needs confirmation.

issue_context.summary: WinUI3Apps executables can show a misleading .NET Desktop Runtime prompt because required self-contained runtime files are missing from WinUI3Apps after some installs or upgrades.
known_information: Affected commands include Settings, Quick Access, and Peek.
Scoop manifest repair was merged and confirmed by one reporter.
A public host trace shows hostpolicy.dll missing during self-contained startup.
inferences: The missing-copy mechanism likely covers package-manager and installer upgrade reports, but exact release coverage is unconfirmed.
issue_context.analysis: The failure occurs before managed UI code runs; the public workaround copies exactly the runtime files the .NET host expects next to the apphost.
initial_investigation: Read live body, comments, labels, events, and timeline through 2026-09-02T21:29:27Z.
Checked origin/main installer generation/custom-action snippets at 5abd20e355998a865075a06676bebfc1d9925be4.
Searched public PRs by related terms; no direct upstream PR surfaced, while the external Scoop PR is linked.

information_gaps.information: Whether the v0.101.2432 reporter has a build containing the WinUI3Apps copy custom action and whether MSI logs show failures.
information_gaps.why_needed: Distinguishes unreleased/already-fixed packaging from still-broken upgrade repair.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Attach installer log or comment /bugreport immediately after reproducing the prompt.

design.root_cause: Missing hardlinks.txt copy repair leaves self-contained runtime files absent under WinUI3Apps.
evidence: Issue host trace and linked hardlinks workaround.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Copies manifest entries when the custom action runs.
implementation_steps.change: Schedule/execute for install, upgrade, and repair; overwrite missing/stale targets.
implementation_steps.code_block: for entry in hardlinks.txt: validate source/target containment; if source exists and target missing or hash differs, copy_file(source,target,overwrite_existing);
tests: Installer upgrade test validates WinUI3Apps runtime files exist.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Builds manifest from duplicate root/WinUI3Apps files.
implementation_steps.change: Fail package validation when required apphost runtime files are neither installed nor listed.
implementation_steps.code_block: assert required runtime/deps files for WinUI3Apps apphosts are in WinUI3ApplicationsFiles or hardlinks.txt;

verify: Install fixed build and launch Settings/Quick Access/Peek.
risks: Installer scheduling can affect upgrade/uninstall behavior.
alternatives: Package-manager-only fix rejected because installer/winget reports exist.

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed reports and host trace. The evidence points to required files from `WinUI3Apps\hardlinks.txt` missing under `WinUI3Apps`. Could someone still seeing this on the latest build please provide the PowerToys installer log, or reproduce and comment `/bugreport` immediately afterward? We need to know whether the installer repair step copied the manifest entries or logged failures.
